title: Cech cocycle description of a boundary class from local lifts
statement: Let X be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let 0 \to I \to O' \to O \to 0 be a short exact sequence of sheaves of commutative O_X-algebras with square-zero kernel I, and let U = {U_i} be an open covering of X. Let f in H^0(X,O) be such that each restriction f|_{U_i} has a lift in O'(U_i), and choose such lifts f_i in O'(U_i). Then alpha_{i_0 i_1} = f_{i_0}|_{U_{i_0} cap U_{i_1}} - f_{i_1}|_{U_{i_0} cap U_{i_1}} is a Cech 1-cocycle with values in I. The canonical map from the first Cech cohomology group of U with values in I to H^1(X,I) is injective, and the image of the class of alpha is the connecting class partial(f) in the long exact cohomology sequence of 0 \to I \to O' \to O \to 0. The same assertion applies simultaneously to any other global section and its chosen local lifts.

source.place: Cohomology, Lemma 0B8R (cohomology-lemma-cech-h1), and Lemma 0B8S proof, paragraph describing the boundary by local lifts

proof.text: By exactness of 0 \to I \to O' \to O \to 0 on each overlap, the difference alpha_{i_0 i_1}=f_{i_0}|_{U_{i_0} cap U_{i_1}}-f_{i_1}|_{U_{i_0} cap U_{i_1}} lies in I(U_{i_0} cap U_{i_1}). The cocycle identity alpha_{i_1 i_2}-alpha_{i_0 i_2}+alpha_{i_0 i_1}=0 is the telescoping sum, which is exactly the degree-one Cech differential relation in [def-weil-pbc-site-cech-complex].

source.place: Cohomology, Lemma 0B8S proof, paragraph beginning 'Let f in R'

proof.text: The compatibility of the Cech-to-cohomology map with the connecting homomorphism is [lem-sc-boundary-cech-compatibility], applied to the underlying short exact sequence of O_X-modules 0 \to I \to O' \to O \to 0. Thus c_I([alpha])=partial(f).

source.place: Cohomology, Lemma 0B8S (cohomology-lemma-cech-h1), compatibility of the Cech representative with the connecting map

proof.text: The canonical map c_I is injective by [lem-sc-cech-h1-injective], whose c_I is the map defined by [lem-sc-cech-h1-map-natural] for the underlying abelian sheaf. Therefore the Cech class is uniquely identified by its image partial(f). The same argument applies to any other global section and its chosen local lifts.
